messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: HIGH severity alert — Dedicated pool 'nimbus-enterprise' (tenant nimbus-sys) experiencing GPU backpressure and queuing. KPI: token-lag > 1200ms p50, 5xx rate rising to 3.2%. Affected routes: /v1/generate (tenant pinned). Paging on-call. pagerduty incident: PD-98377.
jen-oncall: Got the page, I'm on it. Joining zoom in 2.
jen-oncall: Quick check — dashboard shows all 8 GPUs at 98-100% util, queue length spiked from 4 -> 46 in last 10m. No node terminations in last hour.
ryan-enginfra: Looking at autoscaler logs — dedicated pool autoscale policy is disabled for this tenant (policy: manual-only). Confirmed.
nicole-support: Customer (Nimbus Systems) reported degraded latency ~10m ago via support ticket #78921. They're seeing timeouts for some high-concurrency jobs.
sam-pm: Do we have burst capacity allowed for this pool? Contract says burst requires SRE approval + ops-confirm.
ops-runbook: Copy of relevant runbook snippet: `dedicated-pool-burst: requires ops approval -> create temporary-burst token -> route to shared-burst`.
jen-oncall: Options: 1) Enable temporary burst to shared pool (risk: noisy neighbor), 2) Manually scale up GPUs in their dedicated pool (need capacity + infra lead approval), 3) Throttle tenant (protect cluster). Thoughts?
ryan-enginfra: Checking inventory in us-west-2 — we have spare GPUs in reserved pool (2x A100) that can be hot-attached, but that needs change to allocation and a short rolling restart of pool daemons (~3-4m).
jen-oncall: @ryan-enginfra if you can attach, I can coordinate routing change to start using the new nodes.
ryan-enginfra: Preparing command. Will create allocation now.
ryan-enginfra: Runbook command I plan to run:
```
# allocate two GPUs to nimbus-enterprise dedicated pool
infractl pool assign --pool nimbus-enterprise --nodes 2 --flavor a100-80gb --reason "PD-98377 temporary scale"
```
jen-oncall: Doing quick safety checks — confirm model versions pinned? (we don't want any unexpected compat issues when new nodes join).
ryan-enginfra: Confirmed: same image & runtime. Auto-sync config OK.
jen-oncall: ok proceed.
ryan-enginfra: Allocation submitted. infractl shows tasks: attach started. Node join logs: `node-247 joined, runtime ok`.
jen-oncall: Switching routing to include new nodes. Running command to rebalance prefix caches:
```
runtime-admin rebalance --pool nimbus-enterprise --prefetch-kv --drain-warm 30s
```
jen-oncall: Rebalance completed. Queue length dropping: 46 -> 12 over 90s. p50 latency improving to ~420ms.
nicole-support: Notifying customer that we're scaling their pool; asking for any constraints. Message sent. Customer acked: "thanks, we can accept brief restarts".
sam-pm: Good. Is this sustainable or do we need policy change?
jen-oncall: Short term fixed. Root cause: sudden traffic spike from a scheduled batch job at Nimbus that ran an unthrottled fan-out. We need follow-ups: 1) customer rate-limiting suggestion, 2) evaluate enabling burst policy for this tenant, 3) consider autoscale policy update.
ryan-enginfra: I'll leave the temporary allocation for 2 hours and schedule drain after. Leave annotated in infra ticket #INF-4521.
jen-oncall: Filing incident ticket and action items. Posting summary to #incidents.
jen-oncall: Handing off to night on-call @ryan-enginfra (taking over monitoring). Key points: GPUs added, p50 back to 420ms, 5xx down to 0.4%. Customer notified. Keeping temp nodes for 2h.
ryan-enginfra: Taking over. I'll keep an eye on queue and set autoscale flag to alert if we hit >80% again.
jen-oncall: Thanks — going to bed. :zzz:
pagerduty-bot: PD incident PD-98377 acknowledged by jen-oncall.
ops-runbook: Postmortem checklist reminder: capture timeline, customer impact window, commands run, and action owner for autoscale policy.
ryan-enginfra: After 90m observed stable traffic, I'll start a controlled drain of the 2 temp nodes: `infractl pool drain --pool nimbus-enterprise --nodes node-247,node-248 --grace 60s`.
nicole-support: Customer confirms latency back to acceptable levels. Closing support ticket once drain complete.
ryan-enginfra: Drain complete, nodes released back to reserved pool. Pool metrics stable.
jen-oncall: Thanks team. Closing incident PD-98377. Will prepare short incident note: cause = unthrottled batch job, mitigation = temporary scale, action items assigned.
ops-runbook: Incident closed. Please add follow-ups:
- sam-pm: discuss contract-level burst enabling with Sales (owner sam-pm)
- eng-ml: build guardrail to detect large batch fan-outs preemptively (owner: TBD)
- infra: propose autoscale policy change for dedicated pools (owner ryan-enginfra)
jen-oncall: Copying timeline to the incident ticket now. :white_check_mark:
